subject: Proposal: multi-year staged commit with switchback and auto-renew exceptions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Anna Korsgaard <anna@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: multi-year staged commit with switchback and auto-renew exceptions

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attaching a draft term schedule that maps to Nova Retail's expected run rate through the next 24 months and includes:

- A 3-year master term with staged commit buckets (Q1 base, Q3 uplift, Year 2 ramp).
- A one-time "switchback" right in year 2 that lets you reduce committed capacity by up to 20% (with 60 days notice) if usage materially under-indexes the forecast.
- Auto-renew enabled after year 3 unless either party gives 90 days notice; included an explicit exception for price step-ups tied to public cloud costs.

Key asks from our side: confirm target co-term date (you mentioned fiscal July 1), and whether procurement needs a fixed early-termination window on top of the switchback right.

Attachments: Proposed_Term_Schedule.xlsx, Redwood_Terms_v2.pdf

Would love quick confirmation that the structure aligns with your procurement timelines and I'll loop in Marissa to coordinate approvals and pricing floors.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0147

From: Anna Korsgaard <anna@novaretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: multi-year staged commit with switchback and auto-renew exceptions

Marcus —

Thanks for the draft. High level this looks promising. A few clarifying items from procurement:

1) The switchback looks useful but procurement wants a firm cap on how often it can be exercised (e.g., once per 12 months) and a minimal notice window.
2) Price step-ups: can you commit to a cap on year-over-year increases tied to the contract (not just cloud cost passthrough)?
3) We will need a 30-day early termination right in the event of material outage or repeated SLA misses.

Also, can you provide a version of the term schedule that co-terms to our fiscal July 1? We asked for co-terming so all lines align.

If you can send an updated schedule by Fri we can run it through legal.

Best,
Anna Korsgaard
Head of Procurement | Nova Retail
anna@novaretail.com

Subject: Re: Draft: multi-year staged commit with switchback and auto-renew exceptions

Anna —

Appreciate the quick read. Answers below and attached an updated schedule co-termed to July 1 as requested. Changes are highlighted in the spreadsheet.

1) Switchback: we can limit to once per 12-month period with a 60-day notice (so effectively "once/year").
2) Price increases: Redwood can cap direct contract price increases to a maximum of 7% YoY outside of explicit cloud pass-through events — we'll call that out in the term sheet.
3) Early termination for SLA: we will include a 30-day cure period followed by a 30-day termination window if SLA misses continue.

Next steps: I need to confirm discount tiers with Neha for a staged-commit incentive (we had talked about 10% front-loaded credit if you hit the first-year target). Looping Neha on the thread.

Updated attachment: Proposed_Term_Schedule.xlsx (co-term July 1)

Regards,
Marcus

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: multi-year staged commit with switchback and auto-renew exceptions

Marcus / Marissa —

Reviewed the updated schedule. We can approve a 10% front-loaded credit for year 1 (applied as usage credits against committed units) provided Nova signs for a minimum 2-year firm commitment (the remainder can be staged as discussed).

Terms to confirm internally: confirmation that the switchback does not apply within the first 90 days after a renewal/commit uplift (standard guardrail). Also ok to cap YoY increases at 7% with an escape for verified cloud-cost deltas.

If procurement accepts these, Marissa can prepare a final approval note for finance and legal to accept the updated Redwood_Terms_v2.pdf.

-Neha

neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Updated term sheet + requested redlines

Anna —

Attached is the revised term sheet (Redwood_Terms_v2.pdf) reflecting:
- Switchback limited to once per 12 months; not allowed within 90 days post-uplift.
- 7% YoY cap on contract price changes, with documented cloud-cost passthrough.
- 30-day cure/30-day termination for repeated SLA misses.
- 10% front-loaded credit tied to an executed 24-month minimum and first-year consumption threshold.

Note: I've also added a short fallback clause allowing you to reduce reserved concurrency for non-critical workloads without penalty (technical carve-out).

Please confirm and we'll generate a DocuSign envelope; expect a HubSpot update under deal DEAL-78321.

Thanks,
Marcus
